question: Through presidential decrees of 15 August 2026, Türkiye declared two ‘national marine parks’ in the North-eastern Aegean and the Eastern Mediterranean, based on the illegal doctrine of the ‘Blue Homeland’.

These zones extend beyond Turkish territorial waters, include parts of the Greek continental shelf and deny the influence of the islands of Kastellorizo, Samothrace and Lemnos, in violation of international law and UNCLOS. The Commission had already recorded similar declarations in its 2025 Türkiye report and had called on Ankara to respect the sovereignty and sovereign rights of Member States.
Taking into account also my letter of 15 May 2026 to the EU leadership: 1.
Does the Commission intend to explicitly condemn the presidential decrees as acts that violate Greek sovereign rights and are of no legal consequence under international law?
Will the Commission demand the immediate revocation of the decrees and maps so that they are limited exclusively to areas of legitimate Turkish jurisdiction?

Does the Commission consider it compatible with the status of a candidate country to challenge the sovereign rights of a Member State and does it intend to introduce targeted restrictive measures or conditionality?
